quote: And this, despite all skepticism, looks like it’s actually a pretty useful measure of some things, if you ask 100 people and average the results.
content: Averaging is exactly the step that has turned out to be fragile. Self-reported happiness is an ordinal response on a bounded scale; Bond & Lang (2019) showed that for most published comparisons of mean happiness between groups, a monotone rescaling of the underlying variable — equally consistent with the responses — reverses which group is happier. On the other side, some famous threats to the measure have faded: the claim that sunny weather inflates life-satisfaction reports all but vanished in samples of over a million (Lucas & Lawless, 2013). The essay's instinct that the measure is useful for “some things” is right; averaging 1-to-10 answers across groups is one of the things it is least good for.

quote: High schools do nothing but teach to statewide tests.
content: Campbell's law, stated almost word for word and uncredited (Campbell, 1979: “the more any quantitative social indicator is used for social decision-making, the more subject it will be to corruption pressures”). The empirical record is more mixed than “nothing but.” After No Child Left Behind introduced high-stakes state tests, fourth-grade maths scores rose not only on the gamed state tests but on the low-stakes national assessment that nobody taught to (Dee & Jacob, 2011). Gameable measures degrade, and they also sometimes work; the useful question is when.

quote: I consider it drop-dead obvious that the task of verifying acquired skills and hence the power to grant degrees should be separated from the institutions that do the teaching
content: Not obvious, but correct, and already practised. Many countries set curriculum-based external exit examinations; comparisons across countries and across German states find higher achievement where examinations are set centrally rather than by the teaching school (Woessmann, 2005), and British universities have long used external examiners from other institutions to moderate degree classifications. The proposal is a good one with a track record; it would have been stronger for knowing it.

quote: If a hedge fund posts 20% returns, are they really that much better than the indices, or are they selling puts that will blow up in a down market?
content: Exactly right, and the example has a source. Lo (2001) constructed a hypothetical fund, “Capital Decimation Partners,” that did nothing but sell out-of-the-money index puts, and showed that it would have posted a stellar, low-volatility record through most of the 1990s — the kind of record that attracts investors — while carrying a large hidden probability of ruin. The general answer to the essay's organizational-level question is also known for forecasts: a proper scoring rule, under which a forecaster maximizes expected score only by reporting honest probabilities (Gneiting & Raftery, 2007), is a verification method that resists gaming by construction.
